reviews.review: Easily top 5 games ever, maybe even top 3. Just buy it.

It took me awhile to come around to this one, this thumbs up is trending upward but still very sideways. Risk of Rain 1 (RoR 1) was in a different genre (side-scrolling platformer) that I generally prefer over third person shooters. RoR 1 also had phenomenal music; the sequel's is forgettable unfortunately and doesn't seem to hold up to quite the same memorable standard. 

Tthe early stages really feel like a slog to play. I don't know if it's particular to Commando and Huntress, but their initial shooting feels really weak and lacks impact. Huntress at least has her skills to help out, but I quit the game entirely for months because that first run with Commando felt so lifeless. I'm glad that Huntress comes out of the box now so you can at least see what else the game can do, because once you get a few items and become a killing machine, the game shines. But I can't rate this as highly as another roguelite like Hades, which feels good to play from the start.

Other than that, this game retains the same ramping difficulty over time like RoR 1, that emphasizes moving fast through the levels and pacing yourself. That means it also retains the same problem that if you can't find the teleporter, you gain a lot of ramping difficulty for getting lost. This is not everyone's cup of tea, and why I never finished RoR 1 despite liking most other aspects. RoR 2's 3D levels are easier to get lost in, and the time I spent frustrated trying to find the exit pulled me out of enjoying the combat. So fair warning.

All this may sound super critical, but I do think this is a good entry into the roguelite collection. But I don't think it would necessarily be the one I recommend first to others.

Oh, and don't be afraid to turn the game to Drizzle mode. Sure, it's not 'the way the game is meant to be played', but learning the stage layout seems to be key to success.
